sources.entry: ILoveNotch - Turns the MacBook notch into a tray for media, files, calendar, reminders, notes, and timers. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/niyamvora/ILoveNotch) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]
ILoveNotch - Turns the MacBook notch into a tray for media, files, calendar, reminders, notes, and timers.

summary.one_liner: ILoveNotch is a free, open-source, native SwiftUI/AppKit macOS utility that turns the notch on Apple Silicon MacBooks into an interactive tray for media, sound, files, calendar, tasks, notes, timers, network speed and more.
summary.what_it_does: The notch opens on hover, click, two-finger pull-down, or ⌃⌥O, and shows tabs for Media (now playing, controls, lyrics), Sound (per-app volume faders and output switching), a Shelf for dragging files in and out with Quick Look and AirDrop, and a Clipboard history searchable with ⌃⌥V. It also has Calendar and Tasks (Apple Reminders via EventKit, with Join buttons for meeting links), Markdown Notes, Shortcuts, a timer and stopwatch, and Keep Awake. A Network tab shows live download/upload speed and usage history, a Mirror tab shows the camera, and an AI Usage tab tracks limits across 11 AI providers. Agents shows Claude Code and Codex approval and finish states, and Show in Notch displays custom messages via a Shortcuts action or an ilovenotch:// link. The README says the design avoids polling, and some features (Sound, AI Usage, Agents, Android Quick Share) are only in the GitHub build.
use_cases: Control music and see now-playing in the MacBook notch
Turn down or mute individual apps' sound
Keep files on a temporary shelf and drag them out later
See today's calendar events and join video calls from the notch
Manage Apple Reminders and quick notes without opening apps
Track network speed and data usage on a Mac
Run a timer or keep the Mac awake from the notch
Replace a paid notch app with a free alternative
notable: Native SwiftUI/AppKit build with no Electron or webview, aiming for low RAM and near-zero idle CPU
Event-driven design with no polling timers except a few one-shot deadlines and clipboard and network counter reads
Android file sharing over Quick Share on the local Wi-Fi, with no server
Per-app volume control using Core Audio process taps, with no audio driver
Clean-room implementation stated to be MIT, BSD or CC0 sourced; NotchNook's license server going offline is cited as motivation
caveats: Requires macOS 14.6 or later and an Apple Silicon MacBook with a notch; other displays get a menu bar or floating pill version
Mac App Store edition is still in review and lacks AI Usage, Agents, the Sound tab, and Android sharing
Building from source needs Xcode 16+ and Homebrew; the Quick Share support is unofficial and could break with Android updates
keywords: show calendar in mac menu bar
